turns.content: Hello, I received a 12 500 € quote to completely redo my bathroom and the works need to start quickly. How could I finance this amount and within what timeframe can the funds be released?

Your project is clearly identified: the complete renovation of your bathroom for 12 500 €. It is a works project, which comes under an amortising personal loan.

**Can you pay in cash?**

Your available savings amount to 14 695 €. Financing 12 500 € in cash would leave around 2 195 € of reserve, which is low compared with your monthly expenses (around 3 874 €/month) and your current account balance (1 517 €). Paying the full amount in cash is therefore not comfortable here. A mixed solution (part in cash, part financed) remains possible, but a down payment is not required for these offers.

**The offer suited to your need**

For an identified works project, the matching offer is the **Expresso Loan** (amortising personal loan, from 1 000 € over up to 84 months).

**Fund release timeframe**

You mention that the works need to start quickly. The timeframe documented for the Expresso Loan is **8 days minimum**. If your schedule is tighter than that, this timeframe may not be met — I would rather flag it clearly.

**Affordability**

Your current debt-to-income ratio is 20% (956 €/month of existing loan), your average savings capacity is around 928 €/month and your current account balance is 1 517 €. Additional credit remains possible, but you need to avoid harming your remaining income, especially as your emergency savings would be eaten into if you paid part in cash.

**To price it precisely** (monthly payment, total cost, APR depending on the term), I am missing one element: **what repayment term would you like?** (from 12 to 84 months). As soon as you tell me, I will show you an indicative, non-contractual simulation.

In the meantime, you can view the offer and subscribe here:
[URL|Subscribe to the Expresso Loan|https://particuliers.sg.fr/emprunter/pret-credit-consommation/credit-conso-expresso]

If your time constraint is really tight, I invite you to talk to an advisor:
[URL|Book an appointment with an advisor|https://particuliers.sg.fr/vos-rendez-vous]
[RAPPEL|Request a callback from an advisor]
Thank you for these details. The 8-day timeframe worries me a little because the company wants to start quickly. Is there a solution to get the funds faster?

To move faster than the 8 days of the Expresso Loan, only one offer in your selection has a shorter fund release timeframe: the **Alterna Revolving Credit**, whose transfer is stated at **48 hours**.

But be careful: it is not an amortising loan. The rate applies to the amounts actually used, and the total cost is significantly higher. Here is the numerical comparison for your 12 500 €, over a 48-month term used as a simulation assumption:

| Product | Fund release timeframe | Applicable APR (12 500 €) | Monthly payment | Total cost of the loan |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Expresso Loan (amortising) | 8 days minimum | 5.90% | ≈ 293 € | ≈ 1 560 € |
| Alterna (revolving) | 48 hours | 7.90% (on the amount used) | Instalments of 310 to 390 €/month depending on the amount used | Non-amortising: cost depends on actual use |

For Alterna, there is no amortising monthly payment: repayment is made in instalments (for example 310 €/month for an amount used between 7 000 and 10 000 €, 390 €/month between 10 000 and 15 000 €). The total cost therefore depends on how quickly you actually repay.

**My verdict:** your situation remains affordable (current debt-to-income ratio of 20%, positive savings capacity, available savings), but the cost gap between the two options is real. If your company can wait 8 days, the **Expresso Loan** remains the most economical choice. If the 48-hour timeframe is essential, Alterna is the only fast option — provided you accept a higher total cost and non-amortising repayment.

These figures are **indicative and non-contractual**: only the signed loan agreement and subscription are binding.

To start the most economical solution:
[URL|Subscribe to the Expresso Loan|https://particuliers.sg.fr/emprunter/pret-credit-consommation/credit-conso-expresso]

For the fast solution:
[URL|Subscribe to the Alterna Revolving Credit|https://particuliers.sg.fr/emprunter/pret-credit-consommation/pret-credit-renouvelable-alterna]

If you want to decide with an advisor:

Thank you, that is clearer. If I go for the Expresso Loan with the 8-day timeframe, can I ask for a slightly higher amount than 12 500 € to keep a small reserve, or must the loan match the quote exactly?

Good question: the amount borrowed does not need to match the quote to the penny. The Expresso Loan is an **unallocated** personal loan: it does not require proof of purchase, so you can request a slightly higher amount than the quote to keep a reserve. The amount simply has to stay within the limits of the offer (from 1 000 €), and it is your repayment capacity that determines what is granted — the final decision rests with the bank.

To put the impact in perspective, here is an indicative 48-month simulation comparing 12 500 € (the quote) and 14 000 € (with a reserve of around 1 500 €):

| Amount borrowed | Term | Applicable APR | Monthly payment (excluding insurance) | Total cost of the loan | Total amount due |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 500 € | 48 months | 5.90% | ≈ 293 € | ≈ 1 560 € | ≈ 14 060 € |
| 14 000 € | 48 months | 5.90% | ≈ 328 € | ≈ 1 747 € | ≈ 15 747 € |

Assumptions: simulation excluding optional insurance, assuming the application fee from the schedule (0 €), APR of 5.90% for an amount above 6 000 € over 25 to 48 months. These figures are **indicative and non-contractual**: the APR depends on your file and the term, and only the signed loan agreement and subscription are binding.

**Affordability verdict:** the monthly payment of around 328 € for 14 000 € remains in the same order of magnitude as the one for the quote, and your situation (current debt-to-income ratio of 20%, positive savings capacity, available savings) remains affordable. The margin is real, however, but not unlimited: every extra euro borrowed increases the monthly payment and the total cost, so I would advise taking a reserve only if you genuinely need it.

Please note: the fund release timeframe remains **8 days minimum** for the Expresso Loan, regardless of the amount requested.

To start your application:

[URL|Book an appointment with an advisor|https://particuliers.sg.fr/vos-rendez-vous]
[RAPPEL|Request a callback from an advisor]
Understood, so I can ask for a little more than the quote. But concretely, to start the Expresso Loan application, which documents do I need to provide and can everything be done online?

To start an Expresso Loan application, online subscription is indeed available: you can therefore carry out the whole process remotely.

On documents, the data I have indicates that this offer is an **unallocated** personal loan: it does **not require proof of purchase**. You therefore do not have to provide the works quote as a compulsory document. The usual identity, address and income items will be requested at the time of subscription, and the exact list of supporting documents will be confirmed to you during the journey — I cannot detail it beyond what the offer conditions specify.

Two points to keep in mind:

- The fund release timeframe remains **8 days minimum**, including when subscribing online — it is this timeframe that governs your constraint of starting the works quickly.
- The amount you request (12 500 € or a little more to keep a reserve) remains subject to the review of your file: the decision rests with the bank, and online subscription does not guarantee acceptance.

**Affordability verdict:** your situation remains affordable given your indicators (current debt-to-income ratio, positive savings capacity, available savings), with the planned monthly payment remaining in the same order of magnitude as the one for the quote.

You can start the application here:
[URL|Subscribe to the Expresso Loan|https://particuliers.sg.fr/emprunter/pret-credit-consommation/credit-conso-expresso]

If you would prefer to have the documents and the amount validated with an advisor:
